title: Fleet work order (dispatch contract)
description: What a dispatch must say: a target, optionally what to do with it, what authority it carries, where it stops. Generalizes battle-tested operator playbooks into a schema so the delegation contract is enforced, not restated in prose per prompt. Travels with `fleet delegate`. Dispatch shape — `continues` present means adoption, a numeric target means an issue, anything else is prose — is what the CLI keys defaults on and what a repo's pickup gate keys strictness on (#36, docs/decisions.md#d17). Migration window: `mode`, `report` and the unread `authority` subfields are accepted and ignored, and are removed in the follow-up release.

title.description: Human-readable title for the target (e.g. from a GitHub issue). Stamped once at dispatch; viewers never fetch.

target.description: Ticket key, PR reference, branch pair, or symptom statement. An identity, not an instruction: the job branch `fleet/<target>-<jobId>`, the pickup gate's claim guard, `Closes #n`, the board's lineage column and the dispatch shape all read it. `prompt` is where what-to-do lives.

prompt.description: What the operator wants done (#240). The runner uses it verbatim as the harness's launch line, in place of the `/<command> <target>` line Fleet composes from `harness.commands[0]` when it is absent (src/runner/harness.ts buildHarnessCommand). Fleet still appends the continuation clause and the output contract, which are guarantees of the pipe rather than of the instruction. Optional, and the CLI writes it only when asked: this object is `additionalProperties: false` and a deployed daemon validates orders against the schema baked into its own image, so an order carrying `prompt` is rejected outright by a deployment older than this field — `fleet upgrade` before dispatching one. It never decides the shape: strictness, publish and finish come from `target` and `continues` alone (docs/decisions.md#d17), so a prompt naming an issue does not buy a prose dispatch the issue readiness check, and a prompt on an issue target does not escape it.

truth.description: Authoritative sources, in precedence order — VERIFIED at pickup, never assumed. An explicitly named base outranks older specs. Requirements truth and implementation truth that conflict must surface, not silently resolve.

exclude.description: Checked against the diff at settle; a violation fails the implemented rung.

finish.description: Target rung on the evidence ladder. The runner reports the rung actually reached and may never overstate it.

report.description: DEPRECATED (#36), accepted and ignored; removed in the follow-up release. One legal value and no reader — the settle payload shape is owned by the report schema, not requested per dispatch. Status line first (READY/BLOCKED/...), then rung reached vs target, SHAs/PR, verification, self-review, not-done, one exact next action.

continues.description: Post-settle feedback re-entry (#80): this dispatch adopts an existing open PR's head branch instead of creating a fresh job branch. The runner fetches and checks out `branch`, pushes work to it (the PR updates in place), and never opens a new PR. Its presence IS the adoption declaration (#36) — the repo's pickup gate subjects every continues-carrying order to the adopted PR's checks (open, head matches) plus the claim guard, which is where the guard against adoption-by-accident now lives.

branch.description: The PR's head branch, resolved by the CLI at dispatch.

limits.description: Per-dispatch overrides of manifest limits. Merged over the manifest's limits at one chokepoint (src/shared/time.ts mergedLimits) read by both the daemon and the runner.

mode.description: DEPRECATED (#36), accepted and ignored; removed in the follow-up release. The mode string never reached the harness, and dispatch shape now carries what it claimed to: `continues` present means adoption, a numeric target means an issue, anything else is prose. The window CLI still writes it, computed from shape, so an operator repo running a pre-#36 pickup gate keeps gating as it did — see docs/decisions.md#d17.

authority.description: Capability grants — enforced by the broker (tokens), not requested in prose. v1 hard limits: merge and deploy are never grantable. `publish` is the one bit any code reads (the runner gates draft-PR creation on it); `edit`, `jira` and `runtime_read` are deprecated (#36) and removed in the follow-up release.

edit.description: DEPRECATED (#36), accepted and ignored; no reader. A job that can run a harness can edit its own workspace — the enforceable boundary is what it may push, which is `publish`.

publish.description: Push + PR create/update. Read by the runner at settle: false means no draft PR is opened, whatever rung the report claims.

jira.description: DEPRECATED (#36), accepted and ignored; no reader. Tracker capability arrives with a tracker integration, not before it.

merge.description: v1: never grantable. The GitHub token is minted without merge capability.

deploy.description: v1: never grantable. Deploy is out of scope (Post-Build doctrine).

runtime_read.description: DEPRECATED (#36), accepted and ignored; no reader. Runtime evidence is a manifest-level capability question, not a per-dispatch grant.

rung.description: The unified evidence ladder. mergeable is explicitly weak (conflict-free only). merged is a human act (Fleet verifies post-hoc). deployed/runtime-accepted exist on the ladder but are not v1-targetable.

targetableRung.description: Rungs a v1 work order may target. Excludes mergeable (weak, never a goal), merged (human act), deployed and runtime-accepted (out of v1 scope).
